screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intracervical nitroprusside gel versus placebo immediately prior to IUD insertion; primary outcome is subject-reported pain with IUD insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ibuprofen 800 mg versus placebo prior to IUD insertion; measures self-reported pain immediately following insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomised trial of bladder filling versus emptying primarily to assess ease of insertion. The intervention is a procedural positioning technique rather than an intervention specifically aimed at preventing or reducing insertion-related pain, even though pain scores were recorded.

Randomized, open, parallel-group clinical trial comparing intracervical lidocaine injection versus oral NSAID prior to LNG-IUS insertion; evaluates pain immediately, 2 h, and 6 h after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of ibuprofen 800 mg versus placebo prior to LNG-IUS insertion; reports pain with tenaculum placement and with insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind, multicenter RCT of vaginal misoprostol versus placebo prior to IUD insertion; pain during insertion is a secondary outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT of buccal misoprostol versus placebo in nulliparous women prior to IUD insertion; measures perceived pain at tenaculum placement, insertion, and 5 min postinsertion. Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of sublingual misoprostol versus placebo prior to repeat LNG-IUS insertion; reports pain at insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of prophylactic ibuprofen 400 mg versus placebo prior to copper IUD insertion; measures pain immediately after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Single-blind RCT of sublingual misoprostol plus diclofenac versus diclofenac alone before IUD insertion in women with no previous vaginal delivery; pain is listed among the objective outcomes (failed insertion, ease, complications, and pain). Included despite pain results not being detailed in the abstract.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of ibuprofen 600 mg versus placebo before and after IUD insertion; assesses pain during insertion, in the first 4–6 hours, and over the following 3 days. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of oral tramadol versus naproxen sodium versus placebo before IUD insertion; evaluates pain intensity during insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of buccal misoprostol versus placebo before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; measures patient-reported pain immediately prior to and after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel versus placebo before IUD insertion; evaluates pain at multiple time points including insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of vaginal nitroglycerin gel versus placebo before IUD placement; primary outcome is subject-reported pain with passage of the IUD through the cervix. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized trial of 1% lidocaine paracervical block versus no local anesthetic before IUD insertion; measures pain at tenaculum placement, insertion, and 5 min postprocedure. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind controlled trial of lidocaine 2% gel versus lubricant gel versus no intervention in the cervical canal before copper IUD insertion; measures pain during insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intrauterine lidocaine infusion versus saline before IUD insertion; measures pain at tenaculum placement and during insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT of sublingual misoprostol plus diclofenac versus diclofenac alone before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; measures pain at insertion using a visual analogue scale. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of vaginal misoprostol versus placebo before IUD insertion in nulligravidas; assesses moderate-to-severe pain at IUD insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized clinical trial using block randomization of inhaled lavender versus placebo before IUD insertion; measures pain immediately after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT of self-administered misoprostol versus placebo before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; measures pain before, immediately after insertion, and before clinic discharge. Meets all selection criteria.

Phase-II randomized, placebo-controlled trial of a novel topical lidocaine formulation versus placebo for IUD insertion; measures pain during the first 10 minutes and at 30 minutes after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

Prospective, single-blinded, controlled study of paracervical block versus placebo versus no treatment. Randomization is not explicitly stated in the abstract, but the three-arm controlled design with assigned groups is uncertain; included conservatively for full-text review.
Registered randomized clinical trial of misoprostol versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women; primary outcome is pain at insertion via VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of self-administered vaginal lidocaine gel versus placebo before IUD insertion in nulliparous women; assesses pain at tenaculum placement, insertion, and after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
Descriptive clinical report of an intracervical anesthesia technique based on the author’s experience since 1975; no control group and not an RCT.
Prospective cohort study comparing pain during IUD insertion between women with and without a history of vaginal delivery; no randomization to an intervention.
Qualitative interview study of women who have never used IUDs; not an RCT and does not evaluate an intervention for insertion pain.
Narrative review and consensus recommendations article; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
GRADE methodology guideline article; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
ACOG committee opinion/guideline; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Narrative review of pain management for IUC insertion; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Review article on misoprostol use in gynecology broadly; not a primary RCT evaluating an intervention specifically for IUD insertion-related pain.
Observational study comparing expected versus actual pain in a single cohort of nulliparous women undergoing first IUD insertion; no randomization or control group.
GRADE methodology guideline article; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Explicitly described as a nonrandomized study in the abstract; therefore fails the RCT requirement.
Commentary/review article on evidence-based pain management for endometrial biopsies and IUD insertions; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Systematic review of intrauterine local anesthesia for gynecologic procedures; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Observational questionnaire study in which women self-selected oral analgesia prior to IUD fitting; no randomization.
Technical report on contraception for adolescents; not a primary RCT of an intervention for IUD insertion pain.
Meta-analysis of analgesic options for IUD placement; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Randomized controlled trial of nitric oxide donors for cervical ripening before surgical termination of pregnancy in the first trimester; population and clinical context do not involve IUD insertion.
Survey of doctors’ IUD insertion practices; not a randomized controlled trial.
Methodology paper describing the development of a prospective meta-analysis collaboration; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Commentary/review article summarizing controlled trials on misoprostol prior to IUD insertion; not a primary randomized controlled trial.

Randomized double-blind study of meptazinol versus placebo for treatment of pain following IUD insertion over 7 days; evaluates therapeutic management of ongoing pain rather than prophylaxis for insertion-related pain, and falls outside the up-to-six-hours post-insertion window specified in the criteria.
Clinical trial randomly allocating women to lavender, placebo, or control groups before IUD insertion; measures pain during insertion with a visual analogue scale. Meets all selection criteria.
Descriptive article presenting a simplified paracervical block technique; no control group and no randomization described.
Cochrane review summarizing RCTs of NSAIDs for bleeding or pain associated with IUD use; not a primary randomized controlled trial.
